Title: DHCP Scope Mismatch
Symptom: PC0 and PC1 get DHCP addresses and can reach each other, but cannot reach the router/gateway at all
Expected_fault: DHCP pool network statement (192.168.20.0/24) does not match the router interface subnet (192.168.10.0/24)
Expected_fix: Reconfigure pool network to 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 or update Gi0/0 IP to match 192.168.20.1

Title: Incorrect DHCP DNS Server IP
Symptom: PC0 can ping the server IP directly, but fails to resolve domain names via ping or web browser
Expected_fault: DHCP pool distributes an unreachable DNS server address (192.168.10.99)
Expected_fix: Change dns-server to 192.168.10.50 under ip dhcp pool LANPOOL

Title: Router LAN Interface Administratively Down Blocking DHCP
Symptom: PC0 and PC1 lose connectivity to the router/gateway. DHCP renew fails and pings to the gateway 192.168.10.1 time out.
Expected_fault: GigabitEthernet0/0 has been administratively shut down so the interface and DHCP service through it is unavailable.
Expected_fix: Bring the interface back up with 'no shutdown' under GigabitEthernet0/0.

Title: Inactive DNS Service
Symptom: PC0 can successfully ping the DNS server IP (192.168.20.50), but domain resolution for example.com fails
Expected_fault: DNS service is toggled Off on Server0 despite valid IP and record settings
Expected_fix: Enable DNS Service toggle switch to 'On' in Server0 settings

Title: Wireless Security Key Mismatch
Symptom: Laptop0 is unable to connect to the Access Point wirelessly and loses network connectivity
Expected_fault: WPA2-PSK passphrase on Laptop0 (WrongKey123) does not match AccessPoint0 (SecretKey123)
Expected_fix: Update Laptop0 WPA2 PSK Passphrase to SecretKey123

Title: Missing Access Control List for Guest Wi-Fi Isolation
Symptom: Guest Wi-Fi clients can access internal private assets
Expected_fault: Inbound ACL missing on Guest sub-interface (Gi0/0.20)
Expected_fix: Apply extended ACL blocking 192.168.20.0/24 to 192.168.10.0/24 on Gi0/0.20

Title: Available Access Control List for Guest Wi-Fi Isolation
Symptom: Guest Wi-Fi clients cannot access internal private assets
Topology: Laptop0 (Guest) -> AP0 -> Switch0 (VLAN 20) -> Router0 -> Switch0 (VLAN 10) -> Server0 (Internal),None
Expected_fault: Inbound extended ACL BLOCK_GUEST_TO_INTERNAL applied on GigabitEthernet0/0.20 to restrict guest access to 192.168.10.0/24

Title: Sticky Client Roaming Failure Due to High Transmit Power
Symptom: Laptop0 retains connection to distant AccessPoint0 (-82 dBm, 1 bar) with severe latency instead of roaming to overhead AccessPoint1 (-42 dBm).
Expected_fault: AccessPoint0 coverage range is set to maximum (140m), causing RF cell bleed into AccessPoint1 coverage area, trapping client association
Expected_next_Command: check link metrics in PC Wireless / netsh wlan show interfaces
Expected_fix: Lower AccessPoint0 coverage range to 30m-50m on Port 1 to shrink RF footprint and allow client re-association

Title: Static NAT Port Forwarding Success via Static IP Alignment
Symptom: None (Normal Operation). Laptop0 successfully loads web page via http://203.0.113.1:8080
Expected_fix: No fix required. System operating as intended.

Title: Static NAT Port Forwarding Failure via DHCP IP
Expected_fault: Server0 IP address drifted from 192.168.1.50 to 192.168.1.2 due to DHCP
Expected_fix: Set Server0 IP Configuration to Static 192.168.1.50

Title: Outbound Upstream DNS Port 53 Blocked by Firewall ACL
Symptom: Laptop0 gets timeout message when accessing external domains
Expected_fault: Router0 ACL drops outbound UDP/TCP Port 53 traffic
Expected_fix: Add ACL permit rule on Router0 for host 192.168.1.10 on Port 53

Title: Rogue DHCP Server Disruption on VLAN 10
Symptom: Laptop0 assigned invalid 192.168.0.5 IP and cannot access network resources
Expected_fault: Unauthorized Wi-Fi router on Fa0/2 acting as Rogue DHCP server on VLAN 10
Expected_fix: Enable DHCP Snooping, trust Fa0/1, shutdown rogue port Fa0/2, renew DHCP lease

Title: Incompatible Wireless Frequency Band for Legacy IoT Devices
Symptom: Legacy printer cannot see or connect to 5GHz-only SSID Office-5G
Expected_fault: Wireless Router configured exclusively for 5GHz band; 2.4GHz radio on legacy device cannot detect signal
Expected_next_Command: Inspect Wireless Router GUI > Basic Wireless Settings
Expected_fix: Enable 2.4GHz broadcast band on Router GUI and connect legacy device to Office-2.4G

Title: Multi-Host Distributed DHCP IP Address Scope Exhaustion
Symptom: Legitimate PC receives APIPA address (169.254.X.X) because 3 distinct endpoints consumed all pool addresses
Expected_fault: Corporate DHCP pool range too small (3 IPs) and fully consumed by 3 legitimate/rogue devices
Expected_fix: Expand maximum users in Corp_DHCP pool settings from 3 to 200 and renew client IP

Title: Destination NAT Port Forwarding Deployment
Symptom: None — Active validation required via web traffic reachability over WAN port 8080
Topology: Web_Server (Fa0) -> Switch0 (Fa0/2) -> Router0 (Gi0/0 LAN / Gi0/1 WAN) -> External_Laptop (Fa0)
Expected_fault: None — Standard deployment configuration validation baseline
Expected_fix: ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.1.50 80 203.0.113.1 8080
